finding.claim: Broken authorization: deleteAccount calls canDelete() but discards the boolean result, so any caller can delete any account. The sibling closeAccount correctly uses assertCanDelete, which throws.
finding.source: DELETE /accounts/{id}: the id path parameter, sent by any authenticated low-privilege user who does not own the account

trace.note: deleteAccount(User u, long id) is the entry for DELETE /accounts/{id}
The account is loaded by id with no ownership scoping
canDelete(u, a) returns a boolean that is discarded, so there is no throw or return on false

finding.guards_checked: canDelete (line 9-11) is correct logic (admin or owner) but its result is ignored at line 22. assertCanDelete (line 13-17) enforces the check, but it is used only in closeAccount (line 29). I found no other controls on this path. Auth middleware and routing are not in the repo, so I could not confirm authentication.

verdict.guard_found: canDelete (AccountService.java:9-11) returns a boolean, but its result is discarded at line 22. assertCanDelete (13-17) throws, but it is only called from closeAccount (line 29). No other control on the deleteAccount path in the repo. Authentication middleware is not in the repo.
verdict.reason: At src/AccountService.java:22 `canDelete(u, a);` is a bare statement whose boolean result is ignored, so `accounts.remove(id)` at line 23 runs for any caller. Unlike closeAccount (line 29), nothing throws or returns on a false result.
